newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope appeals for talks between Zaire parties.
newsitem.headline: Pope appeals for talks between Zaire parties.

text.p: Pope John Paul appealed on Wednesday for all sides involved in the conflict in Zaire to engage in real dialogue to prevent further suffering.

"I again urge all parties involved in the conflict to accept a true dialogue and real talks and to work together with the efforts of the international community so that an end to hostilities can be achieved as soon as possible," he said.
"Only in this way (by talks) will so many innocent people be spared further and greater suffering," the Pontiff said in a regular weekly address to pilgrims at the Vatican.
He said he also wanted to focus attention on the "tragedy of Rwandan refugees, which seems never-ending".
"I ask for their return home, in dignity, safety and justice, to be favoured with no obstacles or problems or preconceived plans," the Polish-born Pope added.

A meeting between ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and civil war rival Laurent Kabila, which had been planned for Wednesday, has been delayed. Rebels have seized half of Zaire's vast territory since taking up arms in October to topple Mobutu.
